Question
========
Which of the following statements most accurately describes the relationship between an R matrix and an R vector?

Answerlist
----------
* A matrix is a vector that has a `dim` attribute telling R to treat it as having rows and columns; removing that
  attribute turns the matrix back into an ordinary vector.
* A matrix and a vector are completely unrelated object types that happen to share some function names.
* A vector is a special case of a matrix that always has exactly one column.
* Matrices store their data in a fundamentally different way from vectors, using rows and columns instead of a
  single sequence of values.
* A matrix is a list containing one vector per column.

Solution
========
A matrix's underlying data is stored exactly like a vector's — a single, flat sequence of same-typed values. What
makes it a matrix is the addition of a `dim` attribute that tells R how to interpret that flat sequence as having
rows and columns. You can convert a vector to a matrix by adding a `dim` attribute, and convert a matrix back to a
vector by removing it, without touching the underlying data at all.
